ideas.description: Trim the 16 px phase on the tip. Base: E116 code (82e6219). Precondition, free: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 82e6219. Change only the schedule, from 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 to 1.5@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 (6.75 epochs), with switches indexed by samples. Rescale LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence to the new total, as the earlier trims (E070/E088) did. Two anchors stay where they are instead of being rescaled: (a) the whitening-bias detach keeps its position inside the 24 px phase, ~0.97 epoch after the 24 px switch. Plain 41% rescaling would push it into the 28 px phase, where the grad variant is not warmed. (b) The stem + group-1 freeze keeps the same number of frozen samples before the end (~1.09 epochs), so the time saving comes only from the 16 px trim. The final-EMA/lookahead window stays pinned to the last 8 steps. All shapes and variants are already warmed; check with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline (SE ~0.032). Add one scored run with per-trial prepare/train logs.
ideas.expected: Time about -3% (~4.13 s; a bs-1536 16 px epoch costs ~0.26 s, so half an epoch is ~0.13 s). Accuracy: the H8 threshold view predicts ≤0.05 pp loss. My central estimate is -0.03 to -0.10 pp, because E072/E114 suggest half a 16 px epoch might be worth ~0.1 pp. A loss ≤0.05 pp (≤0.017 pp per 1%) makes it the best measured lever: population mean ≥0.7516 stays above the 0.7513 floor, so it can be banked under H4.9 and enters the H2.23.1 combination. A loss ≥0.15 pp (≥0.05 pp per 1%) refutes the threshold view for 16 px exposure and closes low-res trims.

ideas.description: Dose-response of the stem + group-1 freeze at 80% of samples. Base: E116 code. Precondition, free: source hash plus a diff against 82e6219. Change only the freeze point, from 85% to 80% of samples. It stays inside the 32 px / bs-1024 phase, which starts at ~62%. Every freeze x renorm graph and Muon-stack variant is reused unchanged from E116 (already warmed); confirm no recompiles on a 2-trial TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs to measure the real saving. Run a 75% arm only if the 85->80 marginal rate comes in at ≤0.04 pp per 1%.
ideas.expected: Time about -1.5% vs the tip (~4.19-4.20 s): ~0.36 more frozen epochs at ~0.19 s saved per frozen epoch, the rate E116 measured. Accuracy -0.03 to -0.10 pp vs E116 (extrapolating 92%: -0.02, 85%: -0.09 vs E100), i.e. a marginal 0.02-0.065 pp per 1%. At ≤0.05 pp per 1% (loss ≤0.08 pp) the 80% point beats 32 px re-spend and joins the H2.23.1 candidate. Above 0.06 pp per 1%, the freeze stays at 85% and the dose-response is convex.

ideas.description: Early bs 2048 with the warmup fixed in steps. Base: E116 code. Run the 16 px and 24 px phases at bs 2048 instead of 1536. Keep the LR warmup at the tip's step count, not its sample count, which removes E043's warmup confound. Decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, whitening-bias detach (~41%) and the 85% freeze stay sample-indexed. Scale the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) in those phases by the kilostep rule; Muon lr and momentum are unchanged. The 28/32 px phases and the tail are untouched. Compile static bs-2048 16/24 px graphs plus both whiten-bias-grad variants, warm them in build, and verify no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run with per-trial logs.
ideas.expected: Time -1.0 to -1.5% (~4.20-4.22 s): ~27 fewer low-res steps at ~2 ms each. The H8 early-threshold view (E121: +0.004 pp for extra early steps) predicts a loss ≤0.03 pp, i.e. ≤0.025 pp per 1%, cheaper than the yardstick. That would make it a stackable component for the H2.23.1 combination. A loss ≥0.1 pp means large early batches hurt through a channel other than update count (the SGD-bias LR under the kilostep rescale, say), and early batch size closes.

ideas.description: FreezeOut arm (b), with H2.21.3's measurement done in the same step. Base: E116 code. Step 1, untimed: on the 32 px / bs-1024 shape, time with CUDA events and NVML energy over 20 steps each (i) the full graph, (ii) the current detached graph and (iii) a new detached graph in which stem + group-1 BN run in eval mode on the running stats frozen at the freeze point. Log the measured (ii)/(i) saving next to the recounted removed-FLOP fraction including group-2 conv1's dgrad (~18.5%); this settles H2.21.3. Step 2: use variant (iii) for the frozen window (85% onward), as a warmed static graph for every renorm x freeze combination. Running stats stop updating, and eval uses the same stats. Verify no recompiles on a dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run.
ideas.expected: Step 1: H2.21.3 is supported if the measured detached saving is within ±3 pp of the FLOP fraction, and H2.21's bytes claim survives if it is ≥1.2x. Step 2: time -0.2 to -0.5% (~4.24-4.25 s), from dropping the batch-stat reductions over the 31x31x128 maps during ~15% of samples. Accuracy within ±0.03 pp. Train/eval BN consistency for the frozen layers may even give a small gain. If the loss is ≥0.05 pp, train-mode BN in the frozen layers still adapts usefully and the line closes. If the gain is in-noise but the time drop holds, bank it as a free component of the next combination.

ideas.description: Group-3 width 512 as a FLOP lever on the tip. Base: E116 code. Set group-3 width from 576 to 512. Group-3 conv1 input stays 384 and the head becomes [100, 512]. Re-batch the Muon stacks and the dirac init. Warm every (resolution, batch) x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant in build, and confirm no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Untimed first: a per-step profile with the freeze on, projecting total time over the E116 schedule (E117 projected -5.2% with the freeze off). Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Run this after I139 (3/3/2) reports, and skip it if 3/3/2 loses ≥0.45 pp, since group-3 capacity would then be too valuable. Add one scored run only if the loss is ≤0.26 pp.
ideas.expected: Projected time -4.5 to -5.5% (~4.03-4.07 s). The freeze leaves group-3 backward untouched, so most of E117's saving should survive. Accuracy -0.12 to -0.30 pp (low prior: futurebiohackers chose 576 for late capacity, and E005 agrees). A loss ≤0.18 pp (≤0.035 pp per 1%) beats the yardstick and becomes a funded candidate: re-spend ~0.15 epoch at 32 px for a net of about -2.5%. A loss ≥0.26 pp trades no better than a 32 px trim, and group-3 width closes.

ideas.description: Late update count, mirror of E126. Base: E116 code. Step 1, untimed: profile ms/step and NVML energy for static bs-768 graphs at 28 and 32 px, with the freeze and renorm variants. bs 768 at 32 px is ~2.5 waves on 108 SMs, so GEMM efficiency may fall. Project total time. Step 2, only if the projected cost is ≤+4%: run the 28 and 32 px phases at bs 768 instead of 1024, sample-indexed (LR, floor-hold, renorm, the 85% freeze and the Muon x1.25 at 32 px all in samples). Kilostep-scale the SGD groups; Muon lr and momentum are unchanged. Pin the final-EMA window and lookahead stop to the last 8 steps. Warm every variant and verify no recompiles. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled E116 baseline. Add one scored run.
ideas.expected: Time +2.5 to +4% (~4.37-4.43 s), from ~+65 late steps at ~1.7-2 ms each plus some small-GEMM inefficiency. If E126's -0.18 pp is symmetric and comes from update count, the gain is +0.08 to +0.15 pp (central +0.10), i.e. ~0.03-0.05 pp per 1%. At ≥0.06 pp per 1% it is a funding source that beats 32 px re-spend (0.05) and pairs with the freeze or the 16 px trim. At ≤0.03 pp the late-update effect saturates at bs 1024 (concave), and H11.2's update-count reading weakens.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is the E116 code: 4.262 s with a population mean of 0.7521 (~0.08 pp above the H4.9 floor of 0.7513). The measured yardstick is ~0.05 pp of accuracy per 1% of time (E128).

So the plan is to measure the cheap time levers that have not been tested yet, each on the 100-seed instrument, and then combine every lever that trades below the yardstick with 32 px re-spend (H2.23.1).

**Exploit:**
- **16 px trim, 2.0 → 1.5 epochs (H8.3.1, priority 5):** about -3% time at a predicted ≤0.05 pp loss. The whitening-bias detach and the frozen-sample count stay at fixed positions, so the run measures the trim alone and needs no new graph variants.
- **80% freeze point (H2.20.2, priority 4):** about -1.5% more time than the 85% freeze; this measures the marginal rate.
- **Early bs 2048 with the warmup fixed in steps (H2.11.7, priority 3):** about -1.3% time, and it tests the early-threshold view.

**Smaller or explore:**
- **BN eval mode in the frozen window (H2.20.6):** the same run also does the H2.21.3 measurement, comparing the actual frozen-step saving with its FLOP fraction.
- **Group-3 width 512 (H2.19.2):** a -5% FLOP lever, run only after I139 (the 3/3/2 depth cut) reports.
- **bs 768 in the 28/32 px phases (H2.11.5):** the mirror of E126. It tests whether extra late updates can pay for cuts at better than the 32 px re-spend rate.

Already queued: I134 (translate 4, H12.3.1) and I140 (lookahead removal, H9.2.2), so the queue now holds 8 ideas. I139 (3/3/2) is running. Nothing is dropped, because every queued hypothesis is still open.
